title: The First Letter of Peter Timeline
sub: A Living Hope · Suffering Well as Exiles
desc: Written to believers scattered across five Roman provinces, this letter builds an identity as a chosen race and royal priesthood out of suffering itself — following Christ's own pattern of non-retaliation, and ending in a warning about a roaring lion prowling for the careless.

eras.label: Era One · 1 Peter 1
eras.name: A Living Hope — Born Again for an Incorruptible Inheritance
eras.dates: Written to scattered exiles across five Roman provinces, opening in a blessing before a single instruction is given

events.title: Born Again to a Living Hope
events.detail: Peter addresses believers scattered across Asia Minor as elect exiles, opening in praise for a new birth into a living hope through Christ's resurrection — an inheritance kept safe in heaven, tested faith proven more precious than fire-tried gold.

verses.text: “His great mercy has caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.”

events.title: What the Prophets Searched to Understand
events.detail: The Old Testament prophets themselves searched carefully to understand the salvation they were predicting, serving not themselves but a later generation — a mystery so significant that angels long to look into it.

verses.text: “It was revealed to them that they were not serving themselves, but you… things into which angels long to look.”

events.title: Be Holy — Redeemed by Precious Blood, Born of the Enduring Word
events.detail: A call to holiness grounded not in effort but in what's already true — redeemed not with silver or gold but with Christ's precious blood, and born again through a word that outlasts grass and flowers, which wither.

verses.text: “You were not redeemed with corruptible things like silver or gold… but with precious blood, as of a lamb unblemished and spotless, the blood of Christ.”

eras.label: Era Two · 1 Peter 2
eras.name: A Chosen Race, A Royal Priesthood
eras.dates: Identity language borrowed straight from Israel's own vocabulary, applied to a scattered, suffering church

events.title: Living Stones — A Chosen Race, A Royal Priesthood
events.detail: Believers are pictured as living stones built into a spiritual temple around Christ, the cornerstone rejected by builders but chosen by God — language pulled directly from Israel's own identity, now applied to a once-scattered people who 'were not a people' but now are.

verses.text: “You are a chosen family, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God's own possession, so that you may proclaim the excellencies of Him who has called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.”

events.title: Sojourners and Exiles — Submit to Human Institutions
events.detail: Living as exiles among Gentile neighbors, believers are told to keep excellent conduct that silences slander, and to submit to civic authority — not as compulsion, but as an exercise of genuine freedom.

verses.text: “Act as free people, and do not use your freedom as a covering for evil, but use it as slaves of God.”

events.title: Christ's Example — ‘By His Wounds You Were Healed’
events.detail: Instructions to servants suffering unjustly turn into the letter's deepest theological passage — Christ's own silent, non-retaliatory suffering becomes the pattern every believer is called to follow, echoing Isaiah's suffering servant.

verses.text: “While suffering, He was uttering no threats, but kept entrusting Himself to Him who judges righteously. Who Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree… by His wounds you were healed.”

eras.label: Era Three · 1 Peter 3
eras.name: Wives, Husbands, and Suffering for Righteousness
eras.dates: A household code, a call to non-retaliation, and one of the New Testament's most debated single passages

events.title: Wives and Husbands — A Gentle and Quiet Spirit
events.detail: Wives with unbelieving husbands are told their conduct, not their words, may win them over; husbands are told to honor their wives as fellow heirs of grace, since mistreatment hinders their own prayers.

verses.text: “Show her honor as a fellow heir of the grace of life, so that your prayers will not be hindered.”

events.title: Do Not Return Evil for Evil — Always Ready to Give an Answer
events.detail: A call to unity and blessing instead of retaliation, and instructions for believers questioned about their faith — always ready to explain their hope, but with gentleness rather than aggression.

verses.text: “Always being ready to make a defense to everyone who asks you to give an account for the hope that is in you, yet with gentleness and fear.”

events.title: Christ's Suffering, Noah's Ark, and ‘Baptism Now Saves You’
events.detail: One of the most debated passages in the New Testament: Christ's proclamation to 'spirits in prison,' tied to Noah's flood, becomes the launching point for a statement that baptism now saves — explicitly clarified as an appeal of conscience, not a physical washing.

verses.text: “Baptism now saves you—not the removal of dirt from the flesh, but an appeal of a good conscience to God—through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.”

eras.label: Era Four · 1 Peter 4
eras.name: The Fiery Trial — Living for the Rest of Time
eras.dates: A call to redirect the time that's left, and a direct address to a church already facing real persecution for the name of Christ

events.title: Arm Yourselves With Christ's Purpose — Love Covers a Multitude of Sins
events.detail: Having suffered in the flesh, believers are told to stop living for the desires that filled their pagan past and instead use whatever gift they've received to serve one another, since the end of all things is near.

verses.text: “Keep fervent in your love for one another, because love covers a multitude of sins.”

events.title: The Fiery Trial — Judgment Begins With the House of God
events.detail: Peter tells his readers not to be surprised by the 'fiery trial' among them as though it were strange, but to rejoice in sharing Christ's sufferings — and warns that God's own household faces judgment first, before those who reject the gospel.

verses.text: “Do not be surprised at the fiery trial among you, which comes upon you for your testing, as though some strange thing were happening to you. But to the degree you are sharing the sufferings of Christ, keep on rejoicing.”
“It is time for judgment to begin with the house of God; and if it begins with us first, what will be the outcome for those who do not obey the gospel of God?”

eras.label: Era Five · 1 Peter 5
eras.name: Shepherd the Flock — Humble Yourselves
eras.dates: A closing charge to elders, a warning about a prowling adversary, and greetings sent from a church Peter calls 'Babylon'

events.title: Shepherd the Flock — Not for Dishonest Gain
events.detail: Peter, calling himself a fellow elder, instructs church elders to shepherd willingly and without greed, leading by example rather than domination, promising an unfading crown when the Chief Shepherd appears.

verses.text: “Shepherd the flock of God among you, overseeing not under compulsion, but willingly… nor yet as lording it over those allotted to you, but being examples to the flock.”

events.title: Humble Yourselves — A Roaring Lion Seeking Someone to Devour
events.detail: A closing call to humility and vigilance, casting every anxiety on a God who cares, while staying alert to an adversary pictured as a prowling, roaring lion — with a promise of restoration after a season of suffering.

verses.text: “Your adversary, the devil, prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.”
“Casting all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.”

events.title: Closing Greetings From ‘Babylon’
events.detail: Peter closes through his scribe Silvanus, sending greetings from a church he calls 'Babylon' — widely understood as a coded reference to Rome — and from his son in the faith, Mark.

verses.text: “She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you, sends you greetings, and so does my son, Mark.” — 'Babylon' generally understood by scholars as a veiled reference to Rome.
